about: A housing/enclosure benchmark entry (G02, train) in dev.json format, modelled on E1-01. Tier 4: a catalogue module (Arduino Uno R3), two plugs with their cable bodies, standoffs at the board's own holes, openings through a wall (subtraction), a vent pattern, and a screw-closed lid, judged as interference and clearance checks against reference models and keep-out volumes. L1 ids match requirements.md next to this file (L2/L3 tree, reference models, assumptions, fixed decisions, feasibility, traceability). Numbers that are not in the plan brief come from requirements.md section 3. Never put any of these numbers in agent logic: they belong in the request text, requirements, design_rules.json generic values and part.json catalogue data.

methods.inspection: read from the design or mesh (counts, sizes, positions, relations)
methods.analysis: computed by Python (stability, connectivity, interference and clearance against reference models, hand calculations)
methods.demonstration: a stand-in object is placed in the design (fits, rests, does not slide)
methods.test: a probe is applied (insert a plug along its axis, drop the part in, sweep a tool, load path)

requests.title: Arduino Uno R3 case with vented screw lid
requests.request: A case for an Arduino Uno R3 (68.6 x 53.3 mm, four 3.2 mm mounting holes) that sits on four standoffs at the board's own mounting holes. The USB-B receptacle and the 5.5 mm barrel jack are on the same short edge of the board; both must be pluggable with the lid on and their cables attached, so each plug body (the moulded handle as well as the metal) has to fit through the wall. Put a row of ventilation slots in the lid over the ATmega328P, and screw the lid down with four M3 self-tapping screws. The case is a base and a removable lid, printed on an FDM printer in PLA without supports, and the board has to come out for service.
requests.request_notes: Added to the plan brief, all from requirements.md section 3: plug bodies with cables attached (A4); board screws M3 self-tapping into the standoffs (A5); lid is a flat plate in a rebate with four corner-free bosses (F2); FDM, PLA, no supports (A9); board removable (A12).

l1.text: The design shall place the Arduino Uno R3 from the parts catalogue, declare its pose, and put the USB-B receptacle and the DC jack, which are on the same short edge of the board, at the same short end of the case.
The 68.6 x 53.3 x 1.6 mm board shall fit inside the closed case with at least 0.5 mm clearance to every printed surface, apart from where it rests on its standoffs.

The board shall rest on exactly four standoffs, one under each of its four mounting holes, each 5 to 7 mm in outside diameter, with its top plane within 0.1 mm of the others and a pilot hole deep enough for a 10 mm M3 self-tapping screw (through the 1.6 mm board) to seat.
With the lid closed, no part of the case shall come within 12 mm above the board's top surface or 4 mm below its underside, except the standoffs under the holes.

With the lid closed, a USB-B plug (metal shell and moulded handle) shall plug fully into the receptacle through one opening in the end wall without touching the case (at least 0.3 mm clear all round), and that opening shall be no more than 1.5 mm bigger than the plug on any side.

With the lid closed, a 5.5 x 2.1 mm DC barrel plug (barrel and moulded handle) shall plug fully into the jack through its own opening in the same end wall, at the same time as the USB plug and without touching the case (at least 0.3 mm clear all round), and that opening shall be no more than 1.5 mm bigger than the plug on any side.

The lid shall carry a straight row of 5 to 9 ventilation slots (each 1.5 to 3.0 mm wide and 8 to 12 mm long, 3.5 to 6.5 mm pitch) directly over the ATmega328P, with a total open area of at least 100 mm².

The case shall be a base and a separate removable lid: a flat plate that drops into a rebate in the top of the walls (plate 2 to 3 mm thick, 0.15 to 0.35 mm fit gap per side, upstand at least 1 mm) and is screwed down with four M3 self-tapping screws into four bosses in the base.
The closed case shall have no openings other than the USB opening, the DC opening, the vent slots and the screw holes, and its walls, floor and lid shall be 2 to 4 mm thick.
The base and the lid shall each be one manifold body that prints on an FDM printer without supports (no overhang steeper than 45° from vertical, no bridge over 15 mm).
The closed case shall be no larger than 100 x 70 x 35 mm, longest along the board's 68.6 mm side, and shall stand flat on a desk without tipping.
With the lid off, the populated board shall drop straight down onto its standoffs and every board screw shall be reachable with a screwdriver; the lid screws and the board screws shall be separate.
The design shall be delivered as a base STL, a lid STL, the OpenSCAD source, the declared board pose and the agent's own clearance report, and that report shall agree with an independent measurement.
